name: Ottoman Empire

territory.border: hb:1400:Ottoman Empire + hb:1400:Bulgar Khanate + hb:1400:Beylik of Aydin

areaKm2.note: Seshat codes 633,000 km2 for 1440 (low) and 866,000 km2 for 1460 (high); 1453 interpolated. The world_1400 union (Ottoman Empire + its Bulgarian subject + the Aydin beylik absorbed in 1425) measures 520,781 km2, the pre-Ankara state.

population.note: Seshat codes 7.0 million for 1450 and 9.0 million for 1500. Range is a researcher's allowance; vassal Serbia, Wallachia and Byzantine remnants excluded.

urbanization.note: Educated guess. Largest settlement 50,000-60,000 in 1453 (Seshat: Bursa or Edirne).

activePersonnel.note: Standing salaried kapikulu and fleet: 5,000-10,000 Janissaries (archival data via the Fall of Constantinople article; Nicolle has ~6,000 in 1475 via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janissary), Porte cavalry, gunners and armourers (~3,000-6,000, educated guess) and ~10,000 fleet crews and marines (85 galleys, educated guess at 100-150 men each).

trainedReserves.note: Timariot sipahis ~40,000 (Nicolle 1983 pp. 9-10, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janissary), plus azab infantry, akinci raiders and vassal contingents (1,500 Serbian horse). The 1453 siege army is put at 50,000-80,000 in recent studies (archival) and 100,000 by Runciman; western contemporaries' 160,000-300,000 rejected. Counted as feudal levy per the convention.

supportPersonnel.note: Educated guess. Fleet crews (~85 galleys and galliots at 100-150 rowers and sailors), gunners, Orban's foundry men, miners, carpenters (Nicolle 2000: 50 carpenters and 200 artisans improved the roads).

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess. Timar and azab registers plus vassals; ~1.3% of the population reproduces the 1453 siege army.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: Janissaries, 5,000-10,000 in 1453 (archival, via the article). Bowmen with the first hand guns.

quality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: composite bows and early firearms, among the era's best.

count.note: Educated guess. Six divisions of the Porte cavalry (sipahis of the Porte, silahdars).

quality.note: Rubric 0.75: mail and lamellar, composite bow and lance.

count.note: Educated guess. Palace guard infantry (solak, peyk) and garrison troops of Rumelihisari.
~70 cannon at the siege (Lanning 2005, Nicolle 2000, via the article), including Orban's great bombard; 5,000 shots fired with 55,000 lb of powder.

quality.note: Rubric 1.0: the largest siege artillery train of its time.

training.note: Rubric 0.75: Orban and other hired founders.

count.note: Nicolle 2000 p. 44 (via the article): 70 large galleys and 5 ordinary galleys (mid). Contemporary estimates run 110-430 ships including transports (high capped at 110).

quality.note: Rubric 0.5: new-built galleys, outmatched by Genoese carracks on 20 April 1453.

count.note: Nicolle 2000 (via the article): 10 smaller galleys and 25 large rowing boats; 75 horse transports excluded.

commandQuality.note: Rubric 0.75-1.0: Mehmed II built Rumelihisari to close the Bosporus, hauled ships over Galata into the Golden Horn and coordinated round-the-clock bombardment.

cohesion.note: Rubric 0.75: kapikulu slave soldiers with strong corps identity; timariot levy weaker.

morale.note: Rubric 0.75: motivated by recent victories (Varna 1444, Kosovo 1448) and the prize of Constantinople.

weapons.note: Anchor 4-5: great bombards and early hand guns alongside composite bows; between the 1250 and 1600 anchors.

fortification.note: Anchor 4 plus: Rumelihisari (1452) with gun towers.

logistics.note: Anchor 4: menzil road stations, granaries; feeding 60,000 men and 40,000 horses needed ~0.5 million kg of food a day (Military of the Ottoman Empire article).

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (via OWID) Turkey 1450 = 781, 1500 = 768; Greece 1 CE = 1,275 (2011 int$). Balkan provinces with mining (Serbian silver) somewhat above Anatolia.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: Educated guess. Kapikulu salaries from cash revenue plus timar revenues assigned to sipahis; low = peacetime.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess. Bursa silk, mining, arsenal at Gallipoli.

foodSurplus.note: Educated guess. Thracian and Bulgarian grain.

annualCohort.note: population x 0.0095: Hansen 2006 (https://ancientportsantiques.com/wp-content/uploads/Documents/PLACES/GreeceContinental/Athens-Hansen2006.pdf, p. 34) puts a year class of 18-19-year-olds at ca. 1.9% of all males in a pre-modern age structure, i.e. ~0.95% of total population reaching military age per year (males only). Same model as the classical snapshots; medieval age structures were similar (high mortality, young population).

roadKm.note: Educated guess. Via Egnatia, Via Militaris (Belgrade-Constantinople) and Anatolian caravan roads.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess. Gallipoli (arsenal), Thessaloniki, Izmit, Mudanya, Izmir, Enez.

merchantTonnage.note: Educated guess. Black Sea and Aegean trade mostly in Genoese and Venetian hands.

supplyRangeKm.note: Engels (isbn:0520042727, ch. 1) scaled up for the Ottoman menzil station system and pre-stocked depots along the Via Militaris.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Horses, camels, oxen and buffalo, ~0.3 per inhabitant.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.1-1.2: walled cities, local supply; Christian Balkan subjects not reliably supportive.

notes: Snapshot = April 1453, start of the siege of Constantinople. Per the feudal-host convention the timariot sipahis, azabs and akincis of the siege army sit in trainedReserves; activePersonnel is the salaried kapikulu and the fleet. Siege-army estimates: 50,000-80,000 (recent studies, Ottoman archival), Runciman 100,000 (incl. non-combatants), western contemporaries 160,000-300,000 (rejected), all via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fall_of_Constantinople. Agoston (Guns for the Sultan) is the standard modern source on artillery but was not consulted directly. Population convention: directly ruled Rumelia and Anatolia; vassal Serbia, Wallachia and Byzantine remnants excluded.
